$comment: Invariant ids owned by the P2 task `p2-g3-g4-curriculum`: the authored Spanish curriculum, G3 (the constraint solver), G4 (selection + the gap list) and the ledger validators V1-V4 and V9. READ `claim` BELOW BEFORE READING THE REGISTRY ROW: the registry states INV-PACK-06 as 'V1-V4 pass at 100% on the built pack', and on the only pack P2 can build today that sentence is too wide. THE ID IS CLAIMED HERE DELIBERATELY EVEN THOUGH IT TURNS CI RED: the whole ownership apparatus - scripts/coverage-map.ts and packages/core/src/journey/{ownership.ts,phase-roster.test.ts,falsifier-corpus.test.ts} - is TypeScript-only and hard-wired to the P1 roster, so a P2 content invariant cannot be expressed in it yet. Leaving `owned` empty would keep the tree green and leave the invariant unenforced, which the plan's rule 4 calls worse than a failing one. See `blocks` for the assertions that go red and where each is fixed.

blocks.title: scripts/coverage-map.ts cannot see a Python test, so INV-PACK-06 reads as unowned
blocks.detail: THIS LANE'S HALF IS NOW DONE: every test that claims the invariant carries `[INV-PACK-06]` in its pytest NODE ID (via `@pytest.mark.parametrize('invariant', ['INV-PACK-06'])` - a Python function name cannot contain brackets), so `uv run pytest tests/ -k INV-PACK-06` selects exactly the six owning tests and `pytest --collect-only -q` prints the bracketed form. docs/README.md's contract - 'a test whose NAME carries the id in brackets' - is satisfied on the Python side. WHAT REMAINS IS ONE FILE: scripts/coverage-map.ts has TEST_ROOTS=['packages','apps','e2e'] and TEST_FILE_PATTERN=/\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx)$|\.ya?ml$/, and claimedIdsIn() looks for `it('...')` / `test('...')`. None of that reaches tools/coursekit/tests/*.py. Fix: add 'tools' to TEST_ROOTS, add /^test_.*\.py$/ to TEST_FILE_PATTERN, and add one claim form to claimedIdsIn for Python - the simplest that works here is a bracketed id inside any string literal in a file whose name starts `test_`, which matches both the parametrize values and the `"""[INV-PACK-06] ..."""` docstrings. With INV-PACK-06 in `owned` and without that change the job prints MISS and exits 1; with the id absent the invariant is silently unenforced, which the plan's rule 4 calls worse than a failing one. Every C-kind INV-PACK id P2 still owes - 13, 15, 16, 17 - hits the same wall, so it is phase-wide machinery rather than this lane's workaround.

blocks.title: The P1 phase-roster gate has no P2 concept, so four more assertions go red
blocks.detail: The P1 phase-roster gate has no P2 concept. Measured on this branch (2026-09-12): `pnpm test` fails only in packages/core/src/journey/. (1) phase-roster.test.ts 'no ownership file claims an id outside the phase roster' - p1Roster() is derived from P1_FAMILIES plus P1_EXTRA_IDS in journey/ownership.ts, and a C-kind PACK id is in neither, so INV-PACK-06 reads as UNDECLARED. (2) the same file's 'every owned id has an owning test whose name carries the id in brackets' - owningTests() walks TypeScript only (same root cause as ESC-01; the brackets now exist, the scanner still cannot reach them). (3) its counted assertion 'the phase owns what the plan says it owns' - the count is a literal that every new id moves. (4) falsifier-corpus.test.ts 'every owned invariant id has a committed falsifier input' - it requires packages/<pkg>/src/<module>/__falsifiers__/<id>.json, and this invariant's falsifier is a Python one at tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-06.json because the thing it falsifies is a Python validator. All four live in packages/core/src/journey/, another lane's files, and all four need the same two things: a P2 roster beside the P1 one, and ownership/falsifier search paths that include tools/. Every P2 lane that owns an invariant hits this, so it is phase machinery, not a workaround any single lane should write. It must land with or before the P2 integrate; no phase gate can be called green until it does.

blocks.title: tests/test_cli.py::test_discovery_finds_nothing_yet_and_that_is_the_correct_state now fails
blocks.detail: It asserts STAGES.missing(BUILD_STAGE_IDS) == BUILD_STAGE_IDS and VALIDATORS.missing(VALIDATOR_IDS) == VALIDATOR_IDS — true only while no wave-2 lane has landed. This branch registers g3, g4, V1, V2, V3, V4 and V9, so it goes red, exactly as its own docstring predicted ('the day a lane lands coursekit/stages/g0.py this test is the thing that tells them the wiring worked'). It is a tripwire, not an invariant. tests/test_cli.py is outside this lane and EVERY wave-2 lane hits it, so eight branches editing the same assertion would be eight conflicts; integration should replace it once with the complement — every registered id is one config/base.py names, and STAGES.missing(BUILD_STAGE_IDS) shrinks as lanes land.

blocks.title: Registry.reset_for_tests() cannot restore registrations, so one fixture disarms the whole session
blocks.detail: coursekit/__init__.py: reset_for_tests() clears _entries and _discovered; discover() then calls importlib.import_module on modules that are already in sys.modules, which returns them WITHOUT re-running @register_stage / @register_validator. Every registration is therefore gone for the rest of the pytest session after tests/test_cli.py's `empty_registry` fixture runs. Harmless while nothing was registered; now it silently un-registers every wave-2 stage for every later test module. This lane works around it by snapshotting the registry at module import time (see REGISTERED_AT_IMPORT in test_g3_solve.py), which proves the decorators run but not that discovery recovers. The fix belongs in reset_for_tests: drop the sub-package's modules from sys.modules before clearing the flag, or have the fixture save and restore _entries instead of clearing them.

blocks.title: content/es/curriculum.yaml belongs in .prettierignore
blocks.detail: `pnpm format:check` already fails on ~100 files on main and is not a ci.yml step, so this is not a regression — but prettier turns the curriculum from 600 lines into 1,582 by exploding every `target_lexemes` flow sequence to one word per line, which makes a human-authored file unreadable for no gain. `.prettierignore` already carries `content/LICENSE`; add `content/es/curriculum.yaml` (or `content/**/curriculum.yaml`) beside it. That file is outside this lane. content/es/README.md and this file ARE prettier-formatted.

measured.ledger yield (deep/10 Open Question 1): 16.06%, AND THAT IS ABOVE PREDICTED_YIELD_MAX=0.15 - a prediction failure, recorded as one. config/g4.py predicts 5-15% because the framework did; the measurement says 16.06%, so the framework was pessimistic, not the run wrong. Until this commit nothing surfaced that: `within_prediction` was computed, written to the runlog and read by nobody. g4_select.stage_verdict() now says 'OUTSIDE the predicted 5%-15% band' in the stage message and the command below prints the same to stderr; tests/test_g4_select.py::test_a_yield_outside_the_predicted_band_is_stated_in_the_verdict covers above, below and inside. RE-RUN IT, the whole point of this row: `curl -sSLO https://downloads.tatoeba.org/exports/per_language/spa/spa_sentences.tsv.bz2` then, from tools/coursekit, `uv run python -m coursekit.stages.g4_select --corpus spa_sentences.tsv.bz2 --lang es --sample 40000 --curriculum ../../content/es/curriculum.yaml`. It takes ~4 minutes and prints JSON. THE CODE IS COMMITTED (stages/g4_select.py, 'Open Question 1, as a re-runnable command') and lives inside the stage whose admission predicate it borrows, so the number cannot drift from the pipeline; the first version of this figure was measured by a scratchpad script that no longer exists, which is the defect this fixes. Measured 2026-09-12 against the real Tatoeba Spanish export (spa_sentences.tsv.bz2, 6,348,828 B): 441,881 sentences, 387,599 of them 3-12 tokens (87.72%); of a 40,000-sentence sample lemmatised with the pinned es_core_news_md 3.8.0, 6,423 (16.06%) have their whole content-lemma set inside this curriculum's 990-lexeme A1 ledger and 6,387 (15.97%) also exhibit at least one of the 30 authored grammar concepts. Extrapolated over the short pool that is ~62,000 admissible A1 sentences against the ~1,200 a course needs - the Tatoeba-only posture holds for Spanish with two orders of magnitude to spare, and the grammar-concept filter costs almost nothing (0.09pp) because the 30 concepts between them cover ordinary A1 sentences.
measured.es-mini pack: THE PIPELINE REJECTS IT, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT VERDICT. Over the full 30-unit curriculum G4 fills 98 of 756 slots and gaps 658 - gap_fraction 0.8704 against config/g4.py MAX_GAP_FRACTION=0.60 - so g4_select.run() returns ok=False with '658/756 slots (87%) are gaps, over the 60% ceiling. G5 is an authoring stage with a budget, not a way to make a thin corpus look full.' Asserted, with those exact figures, in tests/test_g4_select.py::test_the_stage_refuses_the_es_mini_pack_and_names_the_ceiling and tests/test_validators_ledger.py::test_the_stage_that_built_this_pack_rejects_it_and_the_claim_says_so. The fixture is 200 original sentences written on the same themes as this curriculum, so its own admission rate (134/200 = 67%) is an upper bound and not an estimate of anything. Over that rejected ledger V1-V4 and V9 return 0 blocking findings (3 V2 inflection warnings, 132 V3 recycling warnings, 29 V4 coverage warnings - every one naming the outstanding gap count - plus 42 V3 end-of-course infos); see `claim` for which of those four properties that actually demonstrates and which it does not.
measured.curriculum: 30 grammar concepts, 30 units across 3 A1 sections, 990 target lexemes, no lexeme introduced twice, every concept used exactly once. Against the es-mini lexicon (343 lemmas) G3 assigns 281, back-fills 3 and defers 712 with the deferred list recorded; 84 lessons at 3.3 new lemmas each, under the 7 ceiling.
measured.suite: tools/coursekit: 178 passed, ruff clean (`uv run pytest -q`, `uv run ruff check .`, 2026-09-12). Repo: `pnpm lint` 0, `pnpm typecheck` 0, `pnpm invariants:check` 0; `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:coverage-map` fail entirely from ESC-01/ESC-01b below - see those rows for the exact assertions and the one-file fixes.
measured.V3's N and K are a founder-level choice: RECYCLE_MIN_OCCURRENCES=3 and RECYCLE_WINDOW_LESSONS=12 are NOT in the research corpus. scope2/00 line 127 states the rule as '>=N times within K lessons' and stops; no row fixes either value and the reference product's real spacing was never observed. 3-within-12 is this lane's judgement, flagged as such in config/g3.py, because V3 is the strictest thing in the pipeline - raising N or lowering K makes packs fail - and a number nobody chose on purpose is the wrong reason for that. Revisit with the reviewer sample at the end of P2. By contrast SLOTS_PER_LESSON=9 is deep/01:177 and MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_LESSON=7 is deep/01:419, both cited at their constants.
measured.the two stage ceilings are now tested in: MAX_GAP_FRACTION and CROSS_UNIT_REPEAT_CEILING live in g4_select.stage_verdict(), a pure function the stage returns verbatim, and were previously executed by NO test in either direction - the suite only ever called select(). Now: 60 gaps in 100 slots passes and 61 fails; 5 cross-unit repeats in 100 filled slots passes and 6 fails; both ceilings breached reports the gaps; and one end-to-end run of the real g3 and g4 stages over es-mini asserts run()'s StageResult equals stage_verdict(report), so these are tests of the gate and not of a parallel copy of it.

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: section_cefr is emitted as a G3 OUTPUT derived from which grammar concepts a section contains (R23), and is CHECKED against G2 only where the bands came from CEFRLex. A frequency decile is not a statement about CEFR: checking an A1 label against decile bands would either pass meaninglessly or fail a correct curriculum, so the stage records cefr_checked:false instead — which is what makes a de/ja card read 'Beginner · frequency-ordered' rather than 'A1 · CEFR-checked' (Q8). Both directions are tested.

The A2 prose hole is enforced, not assumed. Only seven cefr_level_prose strings ship (str:2325-2331) and none is A2; the loader refuses an unshippable prose value and CEFR_CHIPS_WITHOUT_PROSE records the chip that has no blurb. This course stops at 'high A1' and never reaches it, but sections 4-8 and the fr/de/ja kits will.

level_count is derived from the published 5-7 new-words-per-lesson budget rather than authored, so the new-item rate holds by construction; _check_new_item_rate asserts the postcondition anyway, because 'by construction' is a claim about code that changes.

Two measured bugs are encoded as named constants with the measurement in the comment. LEDGER_EXCLUDED_POS: with punctuation in the ledger every sentence waits forever on a lemma no curriculum introduces — 0 of 200 candidates admissible, 738 of 738 slots gapped, and the stage reported success. And the loader refuses a non-string lexeme because YAML 1.1 resolves a bare `no` to False, which str() turns into the lemma 'False' — this repository's own curriculum had it.

G4's admissibility index is a watched-literal structure: a candidate waits parked under ONE lemma it still lacks, so introducing a lemma wakes only the sentences parked under it. The obvious rescan is 250k x ~180 lessons of subset tests. Selection is also deterministic by construction (shortest-first then sentence id), because packages/core keys FSRS rows by a content hash and a reshuffled ledger re-keys a learner's whole review history on pack update.

G4 introduces before it practises, and RESERVES a gap slot when a lesson has more pending target lexemes than remaining slots. Without it a unit fills every slot with practice and covers none of its own target lexemes — measured as a V4 coverage failure in unit 29 of the es-mini pack, with no gap slot against it to explain the shortfall.

V2's 'new' means first appearance in course order AND introduction unit == this unit. Without the second clause the rule is unsatisfiable from a corpus: at the start of a course nothing has been carried yet, every sentence looks like five new items at once, and the only ledger that passes is the empty one. Measured: the first working selector gapped all 756 slots for exactly this reason.

V3 and V4's coverage half soften to warnings while a unit still owes G5 gap slots, and the finding names the outstanding count. The falsifier models a FINISHED pack (no gaps) so the same shortfalls block there — which is what makes the softening a scope rule rather than an excuse.

EC-PACK-07 is enforced rather than assumed. validators/ledger.py::_check_segmentation refuses a ledger built on the wrong segmentation for its language (config/g4.py::LEDGER_SPLIT_MODE = {'ja': 'A'}), blocking with no gap-aware softening: a pack on the wrong mode is not an unfinished pack, it is a pack whose validation means nothing. The check is a POSITIVE per-language requirement, so 'es has no modes, split_mode is null' is correct rather than a hole, and that direction is tested too.

No property tests, and PROPERTY_RUNS is therefore vacuously satisfied. The repo's >=10,000-case discipline is a fast-check/TypeScript one and has no Python analogue installed; G3/G4's real properties (no lemma before its unit, <=1 new per exercise, determinism) are example-tested against the 200-sentence fixture plus tmp_path curricula. Not a false claim, but the strongest properties in this lane are single-example tested, and closing that needs a Hypothesis dependency - which is the deps lane's file, not this one.

claim.whyNotWider: The only pack P2 can build is G3+G4 over the 200-sentence es-mini fixture and the 30-unit Spanish curriculum: 756 slots, 98 filled, 658 gaps, gap_fraction 0.8704 against config/g4.py MAX_GAP_FRACTION=0.60, so g4_select.run() returns ok=False on it (asserted in tests/test_g4_select.py::test_the_stage_refuses_the_es_mini_pack_and_names_the_ceiling and again in tests/test_validators_ledger.py::test_the_stage_that_built_this_pack_rejects_it_and_the_claim_says_so). V3 and V4-coverage soften to warnings while a unit still owes G5 gap slots, and in that pack every unit does - so a 'V1-V4 pass at 100%' read off it would be carried by softening for two of the four. 200 sentences cannot fill 756 slots; enlarging the fixture until the pipeline's own gate passes needs thousands of sentences from G0, which is another lane. The claim is stated at the size it is true at rather than the fixture being inflated to make a sentence fit.
toWidenIt: A real es corpus through G0 (>= a few thousand shippable 3-12 token sentences) so gap_fraction lands under MAX_GAP_FRACTION and V3 + V4-coverage become blocking on a pack that passes. That is the P2 gate, not this lane.
A ja kit (SudachiPy + content/ja/curriculum.yaml + a ja corpus) so the Mode-A clause runs on a real adapter. P7.
claim.japaneseHalf: PARTIALLY COVERED, NOT DEFERRED WHOLESALE. EC-PACK-07's mechanism - Mode C glues a compound into one token, V2 counts one new item, passes vacuously while four morphemes reach the learner - is now a blocking check with a test that shows both directions on hand-written rows (Mode C: refused for segmentation, and V2's own count really is 1; Mode A: segmentation clean, V2 fires '4 new lemmas in one exercise'). What is deferred to P7 is running it on a real SudachiPy ledger, because no ja curriculum or corpus exists yet.
